verdict: Monster's sales rose 17% to $2.6B on booming international demand, but rising costs trimmed its margins, so profit grew a slower 8% to $568M.

segments.name: Monster Energy Drinks
segments.note: The core energy drinks — Monster Energy, Reign, Bang and others — sold through bottlers like Coca-Cola distributors worldwide.

segments.name: Strategic Brands
segments.note: Value and regional energy brands, including NOS, Full Throttle and Predator.

segments.name: Alcohol Brands
segments.note: Craft beer and hard seltzer brands (including Cigar City and Oskar Blues) — a shrinking business Monster is exiting; its results are excluded from adjusted figures.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Small remaining sales, including those of the American Fruits and Flavors business.

opex.name: Selling, distribution & other operating
opex.note: Getting cans to shelves worldwide, plus depreciation. Monster reports operating expenses in total and details G&A separately; this remainder includes a $20M impairment on Hawaii property reclassified as held for sale.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Back office, legal and company-wide administration.

otherDetail: Interest and other income, net — Monster sits on a large cash pile and carries no significant debt.
oneTimers: A $20M impairment on land and property in Kona, Hawaii, reclassified as held for sale, sits inside operating expenses. The Alcohol Brands segment also lost $9M at the operating line; Monster's adjusted results (EPS $0.30) exclude both.

takeaways.title: The growth is international
takeaways.text: Sales outside the U.S. jumped 28% to $1.2B — now 47% of the company — while the core Monster Energy segment grew 17% overall.

takeaways.title: Margins are under pressure
takeaways.text: Gross margin slipped to 54.6% from 55.7%, and operating expenses grew faster than sales — which is why 17% sales growth became only 8% profit growth.

takeaways.title: The alcohol experiment keeps shrinking
takeaways.text: Alcohol Brands sales fell 14% to $29M and lost $9M from operations. Monster excludes the segment from its adjusted results as it winds the business down.

footerNote: Figures are rounded to $M from the release's thousands presentation. Monster reports a single class of operating expenses below gross profit; the split shown separates the $306M of general and administrative expense it discloses from the remaining $376M of selling, distribution and depreciation costs.
